A Tesla Cybertruck faces the SpaceX Starship as it sits on a launch pad at Starbase near Boca Chica, Texas. · Bloomberg · Photographer: Sergio Flores/AFP/Getty Images

(Bloomberg) -- SpaceX and Tesla Inc. are progressing in their merger negotiations, setting the stage for a combination that could redefine the limits of global dealmaking.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Alice Huang, Suspected China Spy, Spent Years in Nvidia's Orbit

Alleged Chinese Spy at Heart of Nvidia Scandal Is in Beijing

Nvidia Scandal Creates Risk for Entire AI Industry, Not Just CEO

Mississippi Voters Pick Another Senator to Widen Democratic Win

Nvidia Preparing to Oust Jensen Huang After Affairs, WSJ Says

Elon Musk's two largest companies could announce what would be the biggest-ever deal as soon as in December, according to people familiar with the matter. That aggressive timeline reflects Musk's tendency to move quickly when it comes to corporate maneuvers.

The companies have also discussed a scenario in which an announcement slips into early 2027, said the people, who asked to not be identified because the discussions are private. Their boards and advisers are hammering out the terms of the tie-up and governance structure of the combined entity, among other matters, the people said.

Representatives for Tesla and SpaceX didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Tesla shares jumped to a session high, rising as much as 1.9%, while SpaceX stock gained 0.5% as of 3:20 p.m. Thursday in New York.

The merger would be a blockbuster for Wall Street's dealmakers, creating a conglomerate housing electric vehicles, energy storage batteries, rockets and satellites. The rationale for bringing all those assets under one roof lies in a shared ambition to leverage artificial intelligence across space, driverless cars and humanoid robots.

But both companies will have to grapple with obstacles before they can close a transaction, including how to ring-fence Tesla's operations in China, according to the people.

National security sensitivities around SpaceX's US government and defense contracts, and Tesla's large, profitable China manufacturing footprint, loom as "key dynamics that are at odds with each other" when it comes to getting regulatory and shareholder approvals for a deal, JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta told clients in a research note last month.

The merger would be a major test case for political sentiment following the US midterm elections. Democrats, which took control of Congress, have pledged to probe Musk's business and political dealings.

Musk in October said the boards of the companies had formed special committees of independent board directors to consider combining.

title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: What Do Shareholders Get?
detail:
SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: What Do Shareholders Get?
Lockridge Okoth
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 2:13 PM MST 2 min read
SPCX
TSLA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

SpaceX-Tesla merger talks are progressing, and a deal could be announced as early as December, Bloomberg reported Thursday. Combined, the two companies are worth roughly $3.5 trillion, enough to make it the largest corporate deal ever.

No terms are signed, and the deal could still slip into 2027. For Tesla shareholders, the question is the swap rate, meaning how many SpaceX shares each Tesla share would buy, and at what premium.

What Would Tesla and SpaceX Shareholders Get?

Bank of America analyst Alexander Perry expects SpaceX to buy Tesla with stock, not cash. At a 20% premium, he estimated Tesla holders would own about 47% of the combined company, using October 20 prices. A bigger premium shrinks SpaceX holders' slice.

Tesla stock traded at $393.65 and SpaceX at $140.33 as of this writing. One Tesla share equaled about 2.8 SpaceX shares before any premium.

Elon Musk keeps control either way. Barclays estimates he would hold about 56% of the combined voting power.

Why Tesla's Own Rules Could Still Block the Merger

Musk controls more than 80% of SpaceX's votes. Tesla is harder, because its charter requires a majority of all outstanding shares. Investors who skip the vote count as a "no."

In 2025, that rule sank a non-binding proposal on Tesla investing in xAI. It drew more votes for than against, but 473 million abstentions defeated it. Musk has cautioned against treating this deal as done.

"Some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty... I think that would be overstating it," Musk said.

Bloomberg reported Musk wants the deal closed while President Donald Trump is in office. Democrats, however, won both chambers of Congress on November 3.

Perry named China, where Tesla builds about half its cars, the main regulatory risk, one of the Tesla-SpaceX merger hurdles a former Tesla director flagged.

Will Tesla Shareholders Vote on December 3?

No. Tesla's December 3 annual meeting has no merger item on the ballot. Musk called the merger a good idea in October but recused himself.

Independent committees now set the pace, and any announcement would start the clock on a vote Tesla's charter makes hard to win.

The companies are advancing merger negotiations and could announce a combination as soon as December, Bloomberg reported Thursday, although early 2027 remains an alternative. Their boards and advisers are now working through transaction terms and the governance structure of the combined entity.

The prospect of a merger is hardly new. Musk has publicly discussed the possibility, while the companies have already established closer ties, including their joint Terafab semiconductor project in Texas. But the reported acceleration in negotiations suggests the idea is moving beyond a strategic ambition toward a potentially concrete transaction.

The bigger question is whether the two businesses can be combined without creating significant regulatory and geopolitical complications.

SpaceX's US government and defense contracts carry national security sensitivities, while Tesla maintains a substantial and profitable manufacturing presence in China. Finding a way to ring-fence Tesla's Chinese operations is among the issues under discussion, Bloomberg reported.

Democrats, who took control of Congress following the midterm elections, have pledged to investigate Musk's business and political dealings, potentially bringing additional scrutiny to a transaction involving one of the country's most important defense contractors.

There is also the question of how the deal would be structured. The companies are discussing how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive, alongside the governance arrangements of the combined business.

Strategically, the appeal is clear. A merger would consolidate Tesla's electric vehicles, energy storage and robotics ambitions with SpaceX's rockets, Starlink satellite network and expanding AI infrastructure business. Cash-burn worries are pulling Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID) stock lower as the electric vehicle maker's post-earnings bounce fades. Lucid stock recently changed hands at $3.39, down 8%. That pullback follows a short run to $3.67 by the prior session's close, and it leaves the shares down 68% year to date (YTD).

hapabapa / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

The company still leans heavily on its largest backer. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), the company's anchor shareholder, expanded its delayed-draw term loan facility by $1.75 billion, lifting Lucid's pro forma liquidity to $3.75 billion from $2 billion. Management expects that buffer to fund operations into Q4 2027, bridging to Midsize vehicle production in the second half of 2027.

Lucid's Q3 Cash Burn Keeps Pressure on the Shares

Lucid reported its Q3 2026 results on November 9, missing expectations on both the top and bottom lines. Sales at the company totaled $350.32 million against a $399.14 million estimate, though they rose 4.1% year over year (YoY) while the U.S. battery electric vehicle market fell 41%. On an adjusted basis, Lucid lost $2.30 per share, also missing expectations. Including a $249.91 million accretion charge on preferred stock tied to the PIF, Lucid's diluted loss came to $2.74 per share.
